literal: " Bin, receiving the edict, was greatly afraid; he then led the provincial troops, himself going before the soldiers, attacked the Hu, and pacified them.
idiomatic: Bin took the edict to heart and was terrified; he led the provincial troops in person at the head of his men, attacked the rebels, and pacified them.

literal: In the twenty-third year of Taihe he died.
idiomatic: He died in Taihe year 23.

literal: He was granted one hundred thousand cash and two hundred bolts of silk, posthumously given his former office, and further made Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.
idiomatic: The court granted one hundred thousand cash and two hundred bolts of silk, restored his former rank posthumously, and added Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.

literal: Bin had five sons.
idiomatic: Bin had five sons.

literal: Eldest son: Rong, Prince Zhuangwu of Zhangwu
idiomatic: Eldest son: Rong, Prince Zhuangwu of Zhangwu

literal: (With sons: Jingzhe, Lang, and Huangtou)
idiomatic: (Sons: Jingzhe, Lang, and Huangtou)

literal: The eldest son Rong, style Yongxing.
idiomatic: The eldest son, Rong, styled himself Yongxing.

literal: His bearing was imposing and splendid, his robes and cap very grand; by nature he was open and direct, with a bold spirit.
idiomatic: He was imposing in looks and splendid in dress; open by nature, with a bold spirit.

literal: In Gaozu's time he was appointed Secretariat Gentleman.
idiomatic: Under Gaozu he was made a secretariat gentleman.

literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign his father's enfeoffment was restored and he was made General of Valiant Cavalry.
idiomatic: When Shizong came to the throne his father's title was restored and he was named General of Valiant Cavalry.

literal: Xiao Yan sent generals to raid and press Huaiyang; Liang city fell. An edict made Rong acting commissioner, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and detached commander for the southern campaign; he greatly shattered the enemy host and recovered Liang city.
idiomatic: Liang's Xiao Yan sent generals against Huaiyang and took Liang city. Rong was commissioned as acting commissioner and General Who Pacifies the Barbarians to lead the southern strike force; he broke the enemy badly and retook Liang city.

literal: At that time the Inspector of Yang Province Yuan Song was killed by a slave; an edict ordered Rong to handle Yang affairs.
idiomatic: When Yang inspector Yuan Song was murdered by a slave, Rong was ordered to govern the province.

literal: Soon he was made acting commissioner, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and Inspector of Bing Province.
idiomatic: Soon he was made acting commissioner, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and inspector of Bing.

literal: When Shizong died he was also made Minister of Works and oversaw construction at Jingling.
idiomatic: After Shizong's death he was named Minister of Works and supervised work at Jingling.

literal: He was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan, and with his former rank handled affairs of Ying Province; illness kept him from going.
idiomatic: He was made director of the imperial clan and, retaining his rank, was to govern Ying—but illness kept him from setting out.

literal: Before long he was made Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Inspector of Qing Province.
idiomatic: Before long he was Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Qing inspector.

literal: He returned as Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, moved to Central Guardian of the Army, advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army, took charge as Intendant of Henan, and was further named General Who Campaigns East.
idiomatic: He came back as secretariat supervisor, became central guardian of the army, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army, took Henan as intendant, and was further named General Who Campaigns East.

literal: His nature was especially greedy and cruel; he indulged himself in amassing wealth. The commandant of justice impeached him and his rank and office were struck off.
idiomatic: Greedy and cruel by nature, he plundered at will until the commandant of justice impeached him and stripped rank and office.

literal: The mountain Hu of Fen and Xia rebelled, linking Zhengping and Pingyang. An edict restored Rong's former enfeoffment, made him General Who Campaigns East, with staff and overall command, to attack them.
idiomatic: Mountain Hu in Fen and Xia rose, tying Zhengping to Pingyang. An edict restored Rong's title, named him General Who Campaigns East with staff and overall command, and sent him against them.

literal: Rong was weak in strategy and was defeated by the Hu.
idiomatic: Rong lacked strategy and the Hu routed him.

literal: After a long while he was further made Regular Attendant, General of the Guard, and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Left.
idiomatic: Long afterward he was again Regular Attendant, General of the Guard, and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Left.

literal: Later the bandit chief Xianyu Xiuli ravaged Ying and Ding provinces; Zhangsun Zhi and others campaigned against him and were defeated.
idiomatic: Later the bandit Xianyu Xiuli ravaged Ying and Ding; Zhangsun Zhi and others attacked him and lost.

literal: Rong was made General of the Chariots and Cavalry, forward commander of the Left Army, and with the Prince of Guangyang Yuan Yuan and others jointly attacked Xiuli.
idiomatic: Rong was made General of the Chariots and Cavalry and forward commander of the left army; with Prince Yuan of Guangyang and others he marched against Xiuli.

literal: When the army crossed Jiaojin Ford, Ge Rong killed Xiuli and set himself up as leader.
idiomatic: As the host crossed Jiaojin Ford, Ge Rong killed Xiuli and took command himself.

literal: Shifting camp to the White Ox palisade, light cavalry struck Rong.
idiomatic: Rong's camp moved to the White Ox palisade, where light horse struck him.

literal: Rong fought bitterly all day; with no further outside aid he suffered a great rout and was killed in battle.
idiomatic: Rong fought all day without relief, was utterly broken, and fell in the field.

literal: Suzong held mourning for him in the Eastern Hall, granted eastern-garden funeral gear, one set of court dress, and two thousand eight hundred lengths of colored silk, and posthumously made him Palace Attendant, overall commander of military affairs in Yong, Hua, and Qi provinces, with his former general's rank, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Yong.
idiomatic: Suzong mourned him in the Eastern Hall, granted state funeral gear, court dress, and twenty-eight hundred lengths of colored silk, and posthumously named him palace attendant, commander-in-chief over Yong, Hua, and Qi, with his former general's rank, Minister of Works, and Yong inspector.

literal: Soon, because Rong died in the prince's service, he was further posthumously made Minister of Education, with front and rear guard music added.
idiomatic: Soon, because he had died in royal service, he was further posthumously made Minister of Education with full guard music before and behind.

literal: Posthumous title: Zhuangwu.
idiomatic: Posthumous title: Zhuangwu.

literal: His son Jingzhe inherited.
idiomatic: His son Jingzhe inherited.

literal: In Wuding he was made to open a bureau with Three Precedents parity.
idiomatic: In Wuding he opened a bureau with Three Precedents parity.

literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

literal: Jingzhe's younger brother Lang was the later deposed emperor; his story is in the imperial annals.
idiomatic: Jingzhe's younger brother Lang became the later deposed emperor; his life is in the annals.

literal: His son Huangtou inherited.
idiomatic: His son Huangtou inherited.

literal: He was enfeoffed Prince of Anding, then changed to Prince of Anping.
idiomatic: He was first Prince of Anding, then re-created Prince of Anping.

literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

literal: Rong's younger brother: Ning, Prince of Dong'an
idiomatic: Rong's younger brother: Ning, Prince of Dong'an

literal: (With son: Yanyou)
idiomatic: (Son: Yanyou)

literal: Rong's younger brother Ning, style Dingxing.
idiomatic: Rong's younger brother Ning styled himself Dingxing.

literal: He began his career as Recorder for the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians in Heng Province, and through successive promotions became Chief Clerk to the Guardian of the Army.
idiomatic: He began as recorder on the Heng pacification staff and rose to chief clerk to the guardian of the army.

literal: Ning's paternal aunt was the wife of Erzhu Rong.
idiomatic: Ning's aunt by marriage was Erzhu Rong's wife.

literal: At the beginning of Zhuangdi's reign he was enfeoffed Prince of Dong'an with a fief of five hundred households.
idiomatic: When Zhuangdi came to the throne he was created Prince of Dong'an with five hundred households.

literal: He was made with staff, General Who Pacifies the East, and Inspector of Yan Province; transferred to Inspector of Ji Province, still with his former general's rank.
idiomatic: He was commissioned with staff as General Who Pacifies the East and Yan inspector, then Ji inspector, retaining his general's rank.

literal: In the second year of Yongxi he died; posthumously given staff, overall command of military affairs in Cang, Ying, and Ji provinces, General of Agile Cavalry, and Inspector of Ji.
idiomatic: He died in Yongxi year 2 and was posthumously given staff, overall command in Cang, Ying, and Ji, the rank of General of Agile Cavalry, and the Ji inspectorate.

literal: His son Yanyou inherited.
idiomatic: His son Yanyou inherited.

literal: In Wuding he was Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.
idiomatic: In Wuding he was Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.

literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

literal: Ning's younger brother: Zhan, Prince of Yuyang
idiomatic: Ning's younger brother: Zhan, Prince of Yuyang

literal: (With son: Jun)
idiomatic: (Son: Jun)

literal: Ning's younger brother Zhan, style Zhenxing.
idiomatic: Ning's younger brother Zhan styled himself Zhenxing.

literal: He began as Secretariat Gentleman, became Left Section Chief in the Masters of Writing, [7] and was promoted Vice Director of the Court of Justice.
idiomatic: He began in the secretariat, became left section chief in the Masters of Writing, [7] and was promoted vice director of the Court of Justice.

literal: At the beginning of Zhuangdi's reign he was killed at Heyin.
idiomatic: When Zhuangdi came to the throne he was killed at Heyin.

literal: Posthumously made General Who Campaigns East and Inspector of Qing, and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Yuyang with a fief of five hundred households.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was General Who Campaigns East and Qing inspector, and re-created posthumously as Prince of Yuyang with five hundred households.

literal: His son Jun inherited.
idiomatic: His son Jun inherited.

literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

literal: Ning's younger brother: Yan
idiomatic: Ning's younger brother: Yan

literal: Zhan's younger brother Yan, style Junxing.
idiomatic: Zhan's younger brother Yan styled himself Junxing.

literal: He died while Secretariat Assistant.
idiomatic: He died as secretariat assistant.

literal: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East, Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, and Inspector of Yu.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was General Who Pacifies the East, secretariat supervisor, and Yu inspector.

literal: Prince Kang of Leling, Hu'er
idiomatic: Hu'er, Prince Kang of Leling

literal: Prince of Leling Hu'er died in the fourth year of Heping.
idiomatic: Hu'er, Prince of Leling, died in Heping year 4.

literal: Posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Leling, posthumously made General Who Campaigns North, posthumous title: Kang.
idiomatic: He was posthumously created Prince of Leling and General Who Campaigns North, with the posthumous title Kang.

literal: Heir: Siyu, Prince Mi of Leling
idiomatic: Heir: Siyu, Prince Mi of Leling

literal: He had no son.
idiomatic: He had no son.

literal: Emperor Xianzu ordered the second son Yongquan of Hu'er's elder brother the Prince of Ruyin, Tiansi, to succeed him; he inherited the enfeoffment and later was renamed Siyu.
idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu had Yongquan, second son of Hu'er's elder brother Prince Tiansi of Ruyin, succeed the line; he inherited and was later renamed Siyu.

literal: At the beginning of Gaozu's reign the Rouran raided the frontier; Siyu was made General Who Guards the North and Grand Commander of the Northern Campaign.
idiomatic: Early in Gaozu's reign, when the Rouran struck the border, Siyu was named General Who Guards the North and grand commander of the northern campaign.

literal: Later he was made with full staff, with his former general's rank, Colonel Protecting the Xiongnu, overall commander, and Central Army General.
idiomatic: Later he held full staff, his former general's rank, the colonelcy protecting the Xiongnu, overall command, and the post of central army general.

literal: He went out with full staff as General Who Guards the East, Grand Commander of the He-Long Garrison, and Inspector of Ying Province, further taking the colonelcy protecting the eastern barbarians; he was transferred to General Who Guards the North and acted as Grand General Who Guards the North.
idiomatic: He went out with full staff as General Who Guards the East, grand commander of the He-Long garrison, and Ying inspector, also holding the colonelcy protecting the eastern Yi; he was then transferred to General Who Guards the North and acted as grand general guarding the north.

literal: Gaozu received the hundred officials in the Hall of Luminous Pole and said to Siyu: "The road to Heng and Dai is remote; the old capital weighs on the heart—therefore I have bent my uncle to come far and take this post. You cannot but be reverent and cautious in what you oversee, to fulfill my hope.
idiomatic: Gaozu received the officials in the Hall of Luminous Pole and told Siyu: "The road to Heng and Dai is long, and the old capital still weighs on the heart—so I have asked my uncle to come far and hold this post. Be reverent and careful in all you govern, and do not fail what I expect of you.

literal: " When Mu Tai's secret plot went astray, Siyu knew but did not report it; he was pardoned from death and his enfeoffment was cut back to commoner status.
idiomatic: " When Mu Tai's plot came to light, Siyu had known but said nothing; he was spared execution but stripped to commoner status.

literal: At the end of Taihe his princely enfeoffment was restored.
idiomatic: Late in Taihe his princely title was restored.

literal: In the fourth year of Zhengshi he died.
idiomatic: He died in Zhengshi year 4.

literal: [8] Posthumously made Inspector of Guang, posthumous title: Prince Mi.
idiomatic: [8] Posthumously he was Guang inspector, with the posthumous title Prince Mi.

literal: Son: Jinglue, Prince Hui of Leling
idiomatic: Son: Jinglue, Prince Hui of Leling

literal: (With son: Ba)
idiomatic: (Son: Ba)

literal: His son Jinglue, style Shiyan.
idiomatic: His son Jinglue styled himself Shiyan.

literal: In Shizong's time he inherited the enfeoffment.
idiomatic: Under Shizong he inherited the title.

literal: He was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry, then made with staff, General Who Overcomes the Barbarians, and Inspector of You Province.
idiomatic: He was made General of Valiant Cavalry, then commissioned with staff as General Who Overcomes the Barbarians and You inspector.

literal: [9] In the first year of Xiping he died.
idiomatic: [9] He died in Xiping year 1.

literal: Posthumously given his former general's rank and made Inspector of Yu, granted four hundred bolts of silk, posthumous title: Prince Hui.
idiomatic: Posthumously he kept his general's rank and was Yu inspector, granted four hundred bolts of silk, with the posthumous title Prince Hui.

literal: His son Ba, style Xiubang, inherited.
idiomatic: His son Ba, styled Xiubang, inherited.

literal: In Wuding he was Administrator of Julu.
idiomatic: In Wuding he was administrator of Julu.

literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

literal: Jinglue's younger brother: Qinglue
idiomatic: Jinglue's younger brother: Qinglue

literal: (With son: Zizheng)
idiomatic: (Son: Zizheng)

literal: Jinglue's younger brother Qinglue, Attendant at the Palace Secretariat in Ordinary Service.
idiomatic: Jinglue's younger brother Qinglue was an attendant at the palace secretariat in ordinary service.

literal: His son Zizheng, Regular Attendant in Direct Service.
idiomatic: His son Zizheng was a regular attendant in direct service.

literal: Qinglue's younger brother: Honglue
idiomatic: Qinglue's younger brother: Honglue

literal: Qinglue's younger brother Honglue, Administrator of Hengnong, General of the Central Army, and acting Inspector of East Yong Province.
idiomatic: Qinglue's younger brother Honglue was administrator of Hengnong, general of the central army, and acting east Yong inspector.

literal: Honglue's younger brother: Ziye
idiomatic: Honglue's younger brother: Ziye

literal: Honglue's younger brother's son Ziye, Administrator of Pingyuan.
idiomatic: Honglue's nephew Ziye was administrator of Pingyuan.

literal: Prince Jing of Anding, Xiu
idiomatic: Xiu, Prince Jing of Anding

literal: Prince of Anding Xiu was enfeoffed in the second year of Huangxing, appointed General Who Campaigns South and Grand Master of the Outer Court.
idiomatic: Xiu, Prince of Anding, was enfeoffed in Huangxing year 2 and named General Who Campaigns South and grand master of the outer court.

literal: Xiu was clever from youth and won praise for his judgments.
idiomatic: Clever from boyhood, Xiu was praised for his judgments.

literal: At the beginning of Gaozu's reign the Kumo Xi raided the border; Xiu was made with full staff, Palace Attendant, overall commander of military affairs, General Who Campaigns East, Colonel Protecting the Eastern Barbarians, with Three Precedents parity, and Commander of the He-Long Garrison.
idiomatic: When Gaozu came to the throne and the Kumo Xi struck the border, Xiu was commissioned with full staff as palace attendant, overall commander, General Who Campaigns East, colonel protecting the eastern Yi, with Three Precedents parity, and commander of the He-Long garrison.

literal: Xiu's pacification and defense were well ordered; the bandits then submitted in good faith.
idiomatic: Xiu governed and defended with skill; the raiders then came over in good faith.

literal: He entered the capital as Grand Master of the Central Court.
idiomatic: He entered the capital as grand master of the central court.

literal: When the Rouran raided the frontier he went out with full staff as General Who Campaigns North and Grand Commander of the Fuming Garrison.
idiomatic: When the Rouran struck again he went out with full staff as General Who Campaigns North and grand commander of the Fuming garrison.

literal: Xiu went before the soldiers in person and struck the barbarians, driving them off.
idiomatic: Xiu led from the front, struck the barbarians, and drove them off.

literal: He entered as Grand Master of the Inner Court and was promoted Minister of Education.
idiomatic: He came in as grand master of the inner court and was promoted Minister of Education.
